  "text": "The laundrette clock stopped at twenty past three, though the machines continued turning.

Nina mentioned it when she collected her change.

“Needs a ladder,” Mr Bell said.

There was a ladder behind the dryers, but neither of them looked towards it.

After that, Nina used the time on her phone. She came every Tuesday with two bags, separating the dark clothes on the folding table.

One afternoon, a boy in a school blazer asked when his wash would finish.

“Seven minutes,” she said.

He glanced at the clock.

“That one’s having a rest.”

The boy sat down without smiling.

In December, Mr Bell left a handwritten notice beside the till. His daughter would be running the shop while he recovered from an operation.

His daughter played music and put a bowl of wrapped sweets on the counter. She also brought a new battery.

“Just needs fitting,” she said.

Nina took off her coat.

The ladder was aluminium, its lowest step furred with lint. The daughter held it while Nina climbed.

Behind the clock was a clean circle on the yellow wall.

“Shall I wipe that?” the daughter asked.

“You’ll have to do the rest if you start.”

They put the clock back and watched the second hand move.

When Mr Bell returned, Nina was folding pillowcases.

“You fixed it,” he said.

“Your daughter had the battery.”

He stood beneath it for a moment, then went behind the counter.

The following Tuesday, Nina found the ladder gone from behind the dryers. In its place was a low wooden stool.

“For the high machines,” Mr Bell said.

She set her empty bag on it."
